svg.aria-label: How the exact files and the lossy test builds differ from AMD's FSR 4.1.1 shaders, pass by pass. AMD's shaders: all fourteen passes unchanged, 4.83 ms per frame. Exact files: eleven passes rewritten with the same output, model passes 3 and 6 untouched and pass 11 replaced by AMD's own faster version from FSR SDK 2.4.0, 3.14 ms, the image is AMD's byte for byte. Lossy build on a frame that runs the model: six of the twelve model passes (1, 2, 4, 5, 10 and 12) carry new trained weights, and the postpass skips corrections smaller than about two steps of the picture's number format, 3.22 ms. Lossy build on a skipped frame: all twelve model passes are skipped and the prepass and postpass show mostly the reprojected history, with the model's last result following the motion and the repairs, and nothing taken from the new frame where the picture is at rest unless its content changed, 1.25 ms. The two kinds of frame alternate, 2.25 ms on average, 53% less than AMD's. What the lossy build costs in test scenes at 4K Balanced: still picture 43.89 dB against 44.33, flicker on fine detail at rest 0.080 against 0.110, areas just uncovered by a moving object 37.09 dB against 34.48, brightening 3.7 frames behind against 0.5. The test rig's timing program, 4K Balanced, moving scene, Radeon RX 7800 XT under Linux, one run.
svg.text: Exact files and lossy builds, pass by pass
FSR 4.1.1's passes in the order they run each frame, and what each build does with them.
the model: 12 passes, about 60% of the time
The reference: all fourteen passes as AMD ships them.
Eleven passes do the same arithmetic, laid out so the GPU gets through it faster; pass 11 is AMD's own faster
version from its FSR SDK 2.4.0 (RX 7000 and RX 6000 builds). The image is AMD's, byte for byte.
a frame that runs the model (every other frame)
Six of the twelve model passes carry new weights, trained on this machine to match AMD's picture through this
whole frame loop; the last pass skips corrections too small to matter. The prepass notes each area's motion.
The model does not run, and its last result follows the picture's motion. The picture is almost entirely the
previous one moved along with the scene; the new frame counts for very little, except where the model had asked
for it. Repairs: the history limited to the new frame's colors around the pixel, less weight where the nearest
sample moved away, and the new frame where the history is nearly black, was hidden behind a moving object, or
where the content changed without motion (particles, sparks).
Where the picture is at rest, nothing is taken from the new frame.
Test rig, 4K Balanced, moving scene, RX 7800 XT (Linux)
Test scene, 4K Balanced. Exact files = AMD's.
